# Pi NFT Provenance Verifier — llms.txt
# A read-only, zero-dependency verifier that answers: what happened in this
# transaction, on which ledger, and when — from Pi's public API.

> A transaction hash proves a transaction exists; it does NOT name a person, a
> venue, or an NFT's creator. This tool prints only what the API returned.
> contractId, tokenId and minter stay null unless a Soroban event supplied them.

## What it is
- read-only, zero-dependency, Node (ESM), Node >= 18
- verify.mjs: the CLI (--tx --network --fixture --rpc)
- extract.mjs: ScVal extraction (json + legacy shapes)
- rest.mjs: Horizon REST access
- test.mjs: 29 offline checks (node --test)
- never writes; no database; no API keys

## Source of truth
- Mainnet REST:      https://api.mainnet.minepi.com   (Horizon 28.0.1, Pi Network, protocol 28, history from ledger 2)
- Testnet REST:      https://api.testnet.minepi.com   (pi-horizon 28.0.1, Pi Testnet)
- Testnet Soroban:   https://rpc.testnet.minepi.com   (JSON-RPC, protocol 28, 7-day retention)
- Mainnet Soroban:   rpc.mainnet.minepi.com and soroban-rpc.mainnet.minepi.com -> HTTP 503
There is therefore NO public Soroban RPC on Mainnet. The REST API is the portable
source for transaction data; the testnet Soroban RPC is available via --rpc.

## Why REST and not Soroban RPC
Measured 2026-10-19: Mainnet REST works, Testnet REST works, Testnet Soroban
works, both Mainnet Soroban hosts answer HTTP 503 (certificate expired
2023-05-30).

## Output shape
# Transaction: hash, ledger, created_at, successful, source, fee_charged,
operations, memo. # Ledger: sequence, closed_at, protocol, total_coins.
# Operations: [n] {type, from, to, amount, asset_type}. A JSON provenance record
is printed at the end for machine use.

## Soroban events (--rpc), two measured constraints
- getEvents rejects filter.type = "transaction" ("if set, type must be either
  'system' or 'contract'"), so the tool fetches the ledger range unfiltered and
  matches txHash client-side.
- endLedger is EXCLUSIVE: [L, L] returns nothing, [L, L+1] returns ledger L. The
  tool sends L + 1.
If the response hits 100 events, a truncation warning is printed rather than
pretending it saw everything.

## Usage
- node verify.mjs --tx <hash>                                  (mainnet default)
- node verify.mjs --tx <hash> --network testnet
- node verify.mjs --fixture tx.json                            (no network)
- node verify.mjs --tx <hash> --network testnet --rpc https://rpc.testnet.minepi.com
- node --test test.mjs
Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 bad input (e.g. non-hex --tx, --tx + --fixture); 2 fixture
problems (missing file, JSON array fixture).

## Not claimed
- that a transaction hash identifies a PERSON (the API records accounts, never
  names; attribution is external)
- that source_account is the NFT creator (a mint may be submitted by a relayer or
  marketplace)
- that contractId / tokenId / minter are known from REST alone (they are null
  unless a Soroban event supplied them; null means "not read", not "absent"; under
  --rpc the raw topicJson/valueJson are printed and NO field is labelled tokenId
  or minter)
- that the transaction is the first mint of a token (this reads one transaction,
  not a token's full history)
- that operations/effects are complete for every tx type
- that Pi Network has adopted, reviewed or endorsed this
